races.title: State Assembly, District 6
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Maggy Krell
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 6 (Sacramento) since December 2024. Former deputy attorney general who led the state's Special Prosecution Unit, including the Backpage.com case. Previously chief legal counsel for Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California and a San Joaquin County deputy district attorney.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists 2026 endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, IUOE Local 3, National Union of Healthcare Workers and Equality California.
The Sacramento Bee editorial board endorsed her for a second term, according to excerpts on her campaign site.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Krell was born or raised, or when she moved to California. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. We found no stated positions or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, investor or foreign ownership of homes and land, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site is vague on housing and public safety, and gives no specific policy on these. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or stated positions on data centers or development.

cands.name: Jagtar Singh
cands.bio: Jagtar Singh is a Democratic candidate who ran for California State Assembly District 6 in 2026. He advanced from the June 2 primary and lost the November 3 general election to incumbent Maggy Krell. The sources give no information on his career or offices held.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Jagtar Singh was born or raised, when he moved to California, or what his occupation or work history is. He has held no office that we could confirm. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so there is no record of his stated positions on data centers, property taxes, housing, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no documented deeds, controversies, foreign ties or endorsements for him. The only source available was his Ballotpedia page, which gives election results only.
